title: Bounded-space test and path-count threshold
statement:
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over Boolean symbols, let $x$ be a finite Boolean string, and let $c,B,e$ be natural numbers. If
\[
2^{(2W+2)\left(c\bigl(|\operatorname{bits}(|x|)|+1\bigr)+\operatorname{logSpace}(|x|)+1\right)}\le B(|x|+1)^e,
\]
then the Boolean test on $x$ is true exactly when
\[
2^{B(|x|+1)^e}<2D_{B(|x|+1)^e}\!\left(C_0\right),
\]
where $W$ is the number of bits used to encode a machine configuration cell, $D_t(a)$ is the recursively defined count of accepting computation paths of length at most $t$ starting from configuration code $a$ and retaining only successor codes below $B(|x|+1)^e$, and $C_0$ is the code of the initial configuration with space window $c(|\operatorname{bits}(|x|)|+1)$.
hypotheses_covered: $N$ is a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over Boolean symbols
caveat: The equality uses specialized machine encodings and dynamic-programming definitions, and the given upstream descriptions do not fully specify those functions informally.
